dimensions.explanation: Assess one fund mandate and intended portfolio for a fund manager within paragraph 28. Actor classification is supplied through fund_manager.

Use AMLO section 53ZRA virtual assets, excluding Tokenised Securities under the binding interface. Footnote 7 makes the stated VA objective and intended investment of at least 10% of GAV alternative sufficient triggers; 10% equals 1000 basis points.

Paragraph 28 excludes Tokenised Securities from the selected VA threshold assessment. Its unless clause preserves triggering by qualifying virtual assets; it does not exempt the manager from paragraph 29 or other circular requirements.
The result answers whether the selected trigger applies. It does not establish compliance with the Terms and Conditions or independently predict an imposition decision beyond the selected trigger.

Apply the frozen provision to the stated objective and intended investment, without substituting realised holdings. No assessment date, measurement cadence or later amendment rule is supplied; the 2019 Statement date is historical context.

Paragraph 28 incorporates footnote 7 and refers to the Joint circular, Terms and Conditions and AMLO definition. Their full texts are absent. The interface therefore supplies judgment-dependent actor and asset classifications; separate circular duties are not added as trigger conditions.

questions: What evidence establishes the mandate's stated VA objective and intended VA share of GAV at the assessment point?
For any disputed instrument or actor, how should the cited AMLO definition and Terms and Conditions establish the classifications required by the interface?

assumptions: The supplied interface governs actor and asset classification, including exclusion of Tokenised Securities from both VA inputs.
The assessment concerns one fund mandate and intended portfolio under the frozen 23EC52 provision.
Unknown input facts remain unknown; no actual mandate facts are supplied.

citations.quote: the “de minimis threshold”7 under the Terms and Conditions only applies to virtual assets as defined in section 53ZRA of the AMLO.

the SFC would not impose the Terms and Conditions on fund managers managing portfolios investing in Tokenised Securities meeting the “de minimis threshold” unless the portfolios also invest in virtual assets meeting the “de minimis threshold”.

“de minimis threshold” refers to the situation where either: (a) the stated investment objective of a fund is to invest in virtual assets or (b) the intention of a fund is to invest 10% or more of its gross asset value (GAV) in virtual assets.

readings.distinction: One supported reading is proposed. The objective limb can trigger even below 10% intended VA exposure; the quantitative limb includes exactly 10% and does not require a stated VA objective. Requiring both limbs, counting Tokenised Securities, or adding an actual-holdings condition would lose express qualifiers. The strongest remaining uncertainty concerns supplying the professional classifications and mandate evidence, rather than the disjunction.

facts.meaning: Intended investment in AMLO virtual assets as a proportion of fund gross asset value, excluding tokenised securities; 100 basis points equals 1 percent
facts.name: intended_va_bps

questions: Where the mandate is unclear, what establishes that investing in qualifying virtual assets is its stated objective?
What assessment point and evidence establish the fund's intended VA allocation, given that the excerpt specifies no measurement procedure?
readings.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] The selected VA de-minimis trigger applies to a fund manager within paragraph 28 if either the fund's stated objective is to invest in qualifying virtual assets or its intended qualifying VA investment is at least 1000 basis points of GAV. Tokenised Securities do not count toward either VA condition. A false result means only that this selected trigger does not apply.
